newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines defends destruction of Chinese markers.
newsitem.headline: Philippines defends destruction of Chinese markers.

text.p: The Philippines on Friday defended the destruction of Chinese markers on a shoal claimed by Manila in the disputed Spratly islands

"It's a normal operation," Foreign Affairs Secretary Domingo Siazon told reporters, referring to the demolition of Chinese markers on Sabina Shoal, 120 km (75 miles) west of the southwestern Palawan island, early last month.
On Thursday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang said destruction of the markers was an encroachment on Chinese territory.
"One has to understand that this territory is claimed by everyone, so everyone can put a marker. You remove the marker because (the area) is yours. Nothing extraordinary," Siazon added.
The Spratlys are a cluster of islands, reefs and atolls believed to sit atop huge oil and gas reserves. Beijing says the Spratlys historically belong to China.
The area is also claimed totally or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei and the Philippines.

In April, Manila accused Beijing of sending naval vessels near two islands occupied by Filipinos. Beijing in turn accused Manila of violating China's sovereignty after Filipinos flew their flag over a cluster of rocks called Scarborough Shoal north of the Spratlys.
Last month the Philippines arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near Scarborough Shoal and charged them with illegal entry after rejecting China's demand for their release.
"They will continue to do what they are doing, we will continue to do what we are doing. (But) we will keep talking," Siazon said.
